chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan and Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Is'haq ibn Ammar from Abu al-Atarid al-Khayyat who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The wealth of the orphan is in my possession, so can I trade with it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When you move it, zakat is upon you.' He said, 'I said, 'What if I move it for eight months and leave it for four months?'' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Zakat is upon you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying zakat on an orphan's wealth when a guardian trades with it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the guardian's active utilization ('haraka') of the orphan's wealth triggers the zakat obligation, a principle derived from the concept of nisab and hawl. The specific scenario of trading for eight months and resting for four demonstrates that partial year of activity suffices to establish the duty, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the trustee's agency in wealth management. This ruling ensures that the orphan's assets are not neglected financially, aligning with the broader Quranic imperative to protect vulnerable property.
